target.title: fix(ollama): preserve custom memory provider endpoints
target.body:
Fixes #97055 (residual cache-identity gap)

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and reviewed with Claude.

## What Problem This Solves

The core misrouting from #97055 — custom Ollama memory providers (`ollama-cpu`, `ollama-gpu`, …) being collapsed onto the default `ollama` provider — has already landed on `main` via fa5f24b021e (adapter-side provider-id resolution) and b085184d085 (gateway-side provider-id propagation). This PR has been slimmed down to the remaining gap: the Ollama memory adapter's embedding cache identity is still only `{provider, model, outputDimensionality}`. Two configurations that reuse the same provider id but point at different endpoints (different `baseUrl`, or different non-secret custom headers selecting a different tenant/backend) hash to the same memory provider key and silently reuse stale cached embeddings from the other endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lmstudio memory adapter already keys its cache by `{provider, baseUrl, model, headers: sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders(...)}`; the Ollama adapter now mirrors that pattern exactly (keeping its existing `outputDimensionality` field), so endpoint identity participates in the cache key consistently across local-server adapters.

**Secret-header hardening:** because `cacheKeyData` is hashed into the memory provider key, a credential header in it would force a full reindex on every credential rotation. `sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders` in `memory-host-sdk` now always drops sensitive header names (`authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, and anything containing `api-key`/`token`/`secret`) for every adapter, and `excludedHeaderNames` becomes optional. Secret headers are still sent on the wire — only the cache identity excludes them.

## User Impact

- Users running multiple Ollama endpoints under distinct provider ids (or re-pointing one id at a new `baseUrl`) get correct, endpoint-scoped embedding caches instead of silent stale reuse.
- Rotating a credential header no longer churns the memory index, for any embedding adapter.
- **Compatibility note (maintainer acceptance item):** adding `baseUrl`/`headers` to the Ollama cache identity changes the provider-key hash for existing Ollama memory indexes (including the default `ollama` provider), so they rebuild once via the normal memory index rebuild flow on upgrade. This is intentional — it is required to distinguish endpoints, and memory indexes are rebuildable.

## Evidence

Red-green regression proof — the branch's own test file run on both sides:

**Green (this branch @ `850ea819308`):** `CI=true pnpm test extensions/ollama/src/embedding-provider.test.ts` — all tests pass (31 including the google adapter suite exercising the hardened helper, which passes unchanged — the hardening is behavior-preserving for adapters already excluding their credential headers).

**Red (`origin/main` @ `e43bd3d57bc`, with only the test file copied over):**
```
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > includes outputDimensionality in the memory embedding cache identity
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > preserves custom provider endpoint identity in the memory adapter
AssertionError: expected { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(2) } to match object { provider: 'ollama-cpu', …(3) }
FAIL  ollama embedding provider > excludes secret custom headers from the memory cache identity
```
-> main's cache identity has no `baseUrl`/`headers`, so same-id endpoint changes silently reuse stale embeddings; this branch keys them apart.

`CI=true pnpm tsgo:core` and `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions` are clean.
